audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].side read 'Skill' while content win[6] and the packet chart both read Fizz — the 2+ item row rendered two answers.
audit.why: Veigar has no dash and no escape; Playful/Trickster dodges Primordial Burst outright, so the late row stays yours as long as his stacks were denied.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side moved to Fizz with the why rewritten to argue it; win[6] already reads Fizz, so no paired content edit was needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] (First item) argued the 2-item mark and whys[6] (2+ items) argued the first-item spike — the two rows were describing each other's phase.
audit.why: First item is where your burst rotation kills him before the cage lands; two items is where his stacked Primordial Burst threatens a one-shot and the answer is the pole rather than raw damage.
audit.corrected: Each why rewritten in place for its own row.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] said Dark Matter and Event Horizon are 'both skillshots with long cooldowns'.
audit.why: Event Horizon is 20/18.5/17/15.5/14s — genuinely long. Dark Matter's cooldown is reduced by Phenomenal Evil stacks, so it gets shorter all game, and Baleful Strike is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4. Calling all of it long teaches the wrong step-up rhythm.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] and breakdown.cooldowns now separate the 20s cage from a Dark Matter that shrinks with stacks.

audit.why: Event Horizon 20s at rank 1, Baleful Strike 6s, Playful/Trickster 16s at rank 1, Primordial Burst 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into cooldowns and into dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were tradeGood and tradeBad pasted under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The titles are about poling the centrepiece and respecting feints; the bodies were a generic trade line.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the Primordial Burst dodge and the cage's formation delay.

edits.before: Late Fizz erases one carry per fight: shark the entry, string the target, pole the response, swim away.
edits.after: Late he needs a landed cage to do anything — flank it, pole the Burst, and he has no dash to answer.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage edge and executing with Primordial Burst, which grows on the health you are missing.

edits.before: Fish the strings and respect one spell — his CC is the lane; everything else is water.
edits.after: Fish the strings and respect one spell — the cage is the lane; everything else is water.

edits.before: Shark the rivers: chip, R the entry, string the target, pole the response. One deletion per shark cycle.
edits.after: Chip with W bleed and step off the ring — with no dash, a whiffed cage is 20 seconds of free lane.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Playful / Trickster for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Event Horizon: 20s at rank 1, and only the EDGE stuns — sit near the centre or leave before it forms, and never dash into the wall. - Baleful Strike is 6s. - Dark Matter's cooldown shrinks as his stacks grow. - Playful/Trickster is 16s: emergencies only.

edits.before: If Veigar takes first blood, tighten up: Event Horizon (Cage) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with W last-hits and stay relevant through pole plays.
edits.after: If Veigar takes first blood, every Baleful Strike kill is permanent AP for him — deny what farm you can, last-hit with W, and keep the pole for the cage instead of spending it on the wave.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — shark, string, pole, repeat; one carry per fight is the contract and the pole notarizes it.
edits.after: Carry by hunting the least mobile mage in the game — bait the cage, shark his exit, and string him before it returns.

edits.before: You are the carry-eraser with insurance: shark the backline, string the catch, pole their answer, and swim out of the obituary.
edits.after: He one-shots from behind a cage, so flank it: bait Event Horizon, pole Primordial Burst, and shark him before it recharges.

edits.before: Ahead, fish openly: zone Veigar with string threat, shark every river, and pole the counterplay — fed Fizz makes the map an aquarium.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the stacks: Baleful Strike kills are permanent AP, so take the wave, shark him under tower and keep him off the cannon.

edits.before: Q through him, W bleed, walk out through the wave — the fish phases in and out before his answer finds a target.
edits.after: Playful/Trickster is untargetable — pole Primordial Burst and his 120-second ultimate lands on nobody at all.

edits.before: Veigar whiffs Event Horizon (Cage) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Veigar whiffs Event Horizon and you own the next twenty seconds.

edits.before: That is Veigar’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: A predictable hop is exactly the landing spot he wants to drop the cage on.

edits.before: Hopping in first against a held CC — the pole spent as an entrance is the whole kit spent as a coin flip.
edits.after: Hop only the real cast: the cage takes a moment to form, so walk out of the ring instead of burning 16s.

edits.before: Same logic holds for the 2-item mark — his one-shot needs a landed cage you can just avoid
edits.after: First item burst kills him outright before the cage ever lands, so this phase is yours

edits.before: First item burst lets you kill him outright before his combo ever lands, keeping this phase yours
edits.after: At two items his one-shot still needs a landed cage — and the pole is your answer to that

edits.before: Veigar's Dark Matter (W) and Event Horizon (E) cage are both skillshots with long cooldowns, and once you have E at level 3 you can punish every whiffed cage by closing the gap and slowing him before he resets.
edits.after: Veigar's Event Horizon (E) is a 20-second cage at rank 1 while Dark Matter (W) only speeds up as his stacks build, so from level 3 you punish every whiffed cage by closing the gap and slowing him before it returns.

notes: phases[6].side was 'Skill' against a content win[6] of 'Fizz' and a packet chart of Fizz — moved the full layer and rewrote the why; no win[N] edit needed since content was already right. whys[5] and whys[6] had their phases swapped (the First item row argued two items and vice versa) and are now written for their own rows. spikes[0] called Dark Matter a long-cooldown skillshot; Riot's text says Phenomenal Evil stacks reduce its cooldown, and the kit gives no base number for W, so I described the direction rather than inventing a figure. phases[5].rating is 6/10 while every neighbouring Fizz row is 8/10, which looks stale, but nothing in the kit tells me which is right so I left the row alone per the chart rule.
